title: High-Resolution 3D Spatial Transcriptomics Using Open-ST
author: Schott, León-Periñán, et al.
materials: Timing: 30 min staining, variable time imaging

steps.title: Select and embed tissue
steps.instruction: Choose a freshly frozen tissue sample, embed it in OCT, and verify that the RNA integrity number (RIN) is greater than 7; orient the block to maximise coverage of the future Open‑ST capture area.

steps.title: Pilot pepsin permeabilization series
steps.instruction: Run a pilot experiment comparing pepsin incubation times of 0, 15, 30, 45 and 60 min at 37 °C, assess cDNA yield by qPCR cycle number, and select the shortest time (or lower pepsin concentration) that gives the earliest amplification; refer to Table 1 for recommended conditions (e.g., 30 min for mouse brain, 45 min with 1.4 U/μL pepsin for human metastatic lymph node).

steps.title: Prepare NovaSeq flow cell (Day 1)
steps.instruction: Work in an RNase‑free environment; wash each lane of a NovaSeq 6000 S4 flow cell three times with 150 μL nuclease‑free water; add 150 μL freshly prepared DraI mix per lane (≈150 μL per lane is required).

steps.title: DraI digestion overnight
steps.instruction: Incubate the flow cell at 37 °C overnight (15–18 h) to complete DraI digestion.

steps.title: Post‑digestion washes
steps.instruction: Wash each lane slowly with 150 μL 80 % ethanol, then perform three additional washes with 150 μL nuclease‑free water per lane.

steps.title: Exonuclease I treatment
steps.instruction: Add freshly prepared Exonuclease I mix to each lane and incubate for 45 min at 37 °C; afterwards wash the lanes three times with 150 μL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Open flow cell and denature capture oligos
steps.instruction: Remove the plastic encasing, seal inlet and outlet holes with plate‑sealing tape, and open the flow cell by scoring the sides with a scalpel; then denature the surface‑bound capture oligos by washing both glass surfaces in 800 mL 0.1 N NaOH for 5 min, followed by 800 mL 0.1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 7.5), and a final rinse in nuclease‑free water. Air‑dry the surfaces before scoring.

steps.title: Score and cut capture areas
steps.instruction: Using the 3D‑printed cutting guide and a hand‑held glass cutter, score and break the flow‑cell glass into 3 × 4 mm capture areas (up to ~360 areas per S4 flow cell; maximum piece size 7 × 89 mm). Remove the first and last 1.5 cm of each lane (non‑imaged region). For the thick bottom layer, make six horizontal scores, then vertical scores to obtain 4 mm‑wide slices; each 4 mm slice yields eight 3 × 4 mm capture areas. For the thin top layer, score only the horizontal notches (1–3), place the barcode‑facing side down on a dust‑free wipe, then use a tungsten scribe and the cutting guide to obtain matching pieces. Keep the active (iridescent) side facing up.

substeps.instruction: Measure and mark 1.5 cm from both ends of each lane and cut off.
Score horizontally between lanes (notches 1–3 for top layer, 1–7 for bottom layer as desired).
Score vertically across the lane using the guide and break with a straight‑edged breaking aid.
Separate the glass layers carefully to avoid liquid seeping between them.
Collect the resulting 3 × 4 mm capture areas.

steps.title: Attach capture areas to tape and final wash
steps.instruction: Place each capture area (capture‑oligo side up) onto a piece of cut plate‑sealing tape to facilitate handling; wash the taped pieces once with 100 μL nuclease‑free water before use. The opened flow cell can be stored dry at +4 °C for up to 1 month; capture areas can be stored dry at –20 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Hematoxylin‑eosin staining
steps.instruction: Perform H&E staining on the tissue sections mounted on the capture areas: remove the areas from cold methanol, add isopropanol and incubate 1 min, tilt to dry (~1 min) until matte, add hematoxylin and incubate 5 min, wash 10–15× with nuclease‑free water, add bluing buffer and incubate 2 min, wash 5×, add buffered eosin Y and incubate 1 min, wash 10–15×, air‑dry 10 min at room temperature, then carefully remove the tape with pointy tweezers.

steps.title: Image stained sections
steps.instruction: Image the stained capture area on a bright‑field microscope using a 20× objective (PlanApo λ 20× 0.75/1.00 mm) with the settings: 100 % brightfield, 20 % aperture stop, no oblique illumination, high‑resolution mode; typical imaging time is 2–5 min per 3 × 4 mm area. After imaging, place the capture areas (tissue‑side up) into microarray chamber wells.

steps.title: Second‑strand cDNA synthesis
steps.instruction: Add 100 μL second‑strand synthesis mix to each capture area chamber, seal, and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h; then wash the chamber three times with 100 μL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Elute second strand with NaOH
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 N NaOH freshly from a 1 N or 10 N stock; add 100 μL 0.1 N NaOH to each capture‑area chamber and incubate 5 min; recover the eluate into a LoBind tube, repeat once and pool the two 100 μL eluates (total ~200 μL).

steps.title: Neutralize eluate
steps.instruction: Add 28.6 μL of 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 7.5) to each 200 μL of second‑strand eluate to neutralise the NaOH.

steps.title: Purify second strand with Ampure XP beads
steps.instruction: Bring Ampure XP beads to room temperature for 30 min, vortex, then add 411 μL beads (1.8 × volume) to the 228.6 μL eluate; mix by pipetting 10 ×, incubate 10 min at room temperature, place on a magnetic rack for 5 min, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 1 mL 80 % ethanol (30 s each), remove residual ethanol, air‑dry beads 5 min (avoid over‑drying), resuspend in 82.5 μL nuclease‑free water (pipet 10 ×), incubate 5 min, magnetise 30 s, and collect the 82.5 μL purified second‑strand cDNA.

steps.title: Store purified second strand
steps.instruction: Store the purified second‑strand cDNA at –20 °C or –80 °C for up to 1 year; optionally, keep the original capture areas dry at –20 °C after washing twice with 100 μL 0.1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 7.5) and twice with 100 μL nuclease‑free water.

description: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has emerged as a crucial tool for understanding the complex organization of tissues in health and disease, revealing how the spatial arrangement of cells and their gene expression patterns contribute to organ function and pathology. Open-ST addresses this need by providing a cost-effective method for whole-transcriptome capture at subcellular resolution, by converting patterned Illumina flow cells into ST capture areas with ∼0.6 μm barcoded spots. This enables the study of diverse tissue types from tumor microenvironments to structured organs, in 2D and 3D. Importantly, Open-ST is a fully open-source and adaptable resource for researchers across various fields of biology and medicine. This protocol covers the implementation of Open-ST. The workflow covers (1) generating capture areas, (2) preparing libraries, and (3) analyzing data in both 2D and 3D contexts, including the reconstruction of 3D "virtual tissue blocks" from serial sections. We demonstrate the protocol using human metastatic lymph node tissue from a head and neck squamous cell carcinoma patient, showcasing Open-ST’s capabilities from 2D sections to a 3D reconstruction from serial sections. The method has been applied to diverse tissues, including mouse embryonic head, adult mouse hippocampus, and various human clinical samples,1 and can be applied to any species. Before you begin, we recommend carefully selecting your tissue sample: tissue must be freshly frozen and embedded in OCT. The RNA quality, expressed as the RNA integrity number (RIN), should ideally be > 7. Furthermore, choose and embed your tissue to maximize the tissue coverage of your Open-ST capture area, in order to increase library input. We advise a pilot experiment to compare different permeabilization conditions using a qPCR assay. We suggest comparing different pepsin incubation times (for example, 0, 15, 30, 45, and 60 min) at 37°C. For permeabilization optimization, follow the library preparation steps
